desc: Ideate candidate approaches and select backward capped-run DP with greedy lexicographic reconstruction.

Implement and validate the complete backward capped-run DP solution in `Solution.minCostGoodCaption`: return "" for n<3; define dp1/dp2/dp3[i][c] as the min suffix cost from position i given an open previous run of c with capped length 1/2/3; use base dp3[n][c]=0 and dp1/dp2[n][c]=INF; fill i=n-1..0 with dp1[i][c]=cost(i,c)+dp2[i+1][c], dp2[i][c]=cost(i,c)+dp3[i+1][c], and dp3[i][c]=min(cost(i,c)+dp3[i+1][c], min_{x!=c} cost(i,x)+dp1[i+1][x]) using per-position smallest/second-smallest A[x]=cost(i,x)+dp1[i+1][x]; compute total=min_x cost(0,x)+dp1[1][x]; then greedily reconstruct the lexicographically smallest optimal string by trying letters 'a'..'z' at each position and accepting the first valid transition whose cost plus the stored next-state DP equals the remaining optimal cost; use compact arrays and test the provided examples plus small brute-force/edge cases.
If validation fails, switch to a different exact approach (forward rank-compressed DP) or use the block/run-boundary DP as a cost oracle to debug/replace the solution.
